_comment_family: Kallisto ships as a family and this file is its Medium, the cut the
Experts React captions are set in. The name needs the same care the
two Telegraf packs take: the Heavy sits in fonts/ beside it, and the
two are far enough apart (500 against 900) that a title measured
against one and drawn in the other is not a different look, it is a
There is less to fix here than in those packs, because the file has
already been split the way they split it by hand: its Windows records
carry 'Kallisto Medium' as name ID 1 and as the full name ID 4, with
the bare 'Kallisto' left in the typographic family (ID 16) and the cut
in ID 17. So the name declared here is both the family and the full
name, it answers with this one cut whichever of the two a browser
matches on, and the Heavy beside it cannot answer to it.
Weight 500, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Stated rather than left to 'normal' so the fallbacks below
resolve to the nearest weight of their own family rather than to
whatever a browser picks when it is asked for nothing in particular.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4) and the second the
PostScript name (ID 6); both name this one cut rather than a family
with cuts in it, so a machine answering to either is answering with
The first is also the name the installer registers the face under -
it copies each pack's font into the user's font folder and keys it by
local[0] (see engine.install_fonts), and Windows keys installed fonts
by their full name. So this list being in this order is what makes
the installed copy findable by the stack below.
'Kallisto' on its own is deliberately absent: it is the typographic
family, and the Heavy answers to it as well.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and the thing they
were chosen against is width: Kallisto is a wide squarish techno sans
whose capitals average 0.753em, which is the widest block face under
the Snapchat heading - wider than Montserrat SemiBold at 0.728 and
than Telegraf UltraLight at 0.660.
What the machine can be relied on to have, measured the same way:
Verdana 0.687em, Arial 0.677, Segoe UI 0.613, Century Gothic 0.638.
Verdana is the closest of them at 9% narrower, and it is also the
nearest in manner - the widest, most open-shouldered face on a stock
Windows, with squared-off terminals where the others curl. Segoe UI
and Arial stand behind it, each a little narrower and each a caption
that has gained a word on a line rather than one that has lost its
face entirely.
A narrower substitute is the safe direction here, and that is why
width leads the choice rather than settles it. The caption is wrapped
in whatever face actually loaded (see captionLines in js/caption.js),
so a narrower one fits more words to a line and makes a shorter card
- where korolev-bold, wrapped once against a face that did load,
would have run its lines off the frame.
Impact and Arial Black are absent for telegraf-ultralight's reason:
they are heavy display cuts, and putting one behind a 500-weight face
would make the one thing that survives a missing file the furthest
possible thing from it. Century Gothic is absent for a second reason
besides its width - it is built on true circles, and Kallisto's round
shapes are flattened at the sides, so it resembles this face in the
one respect a reader sees first and would resemble it wrongly.
